Hi Elena — great to hear. Short answers up front: yes, we can support split invoicing to multiple legal entities; and we’ll need VAT/residency documentation to determine chargeability and withholding.

Next steps I recommend:
- We’ll route subscription invoices to SkyForge, Inc. (US) and PS/activation to SkyForge Ltd (EMEA) — please confirm the exact legal names and remit-to addresses.
- Finance will need either a VAT registration certificate (for EU entity) or a W-9/W-8 for US tax residency; if withholding applies we’ll capture that via the order form appendix.
- Ben, can you propose a clean commercial redline for the order form to capture the split-invoice flow + a net-terms fallback?
- Kimberly / Lauren, tagging legal and finance ops for any procurement/PO expectations.

We’ll keep the draft order form as the single source of truth and add an invoice-routing appendix. I attached an initial pricing schedule spreadsheet with the staged minimum commits so you can see the proposed phasing.

Subject: Re: Order Form: commercial terms & invoicing entity question

Elena — thanks for flagging. I’ve sketched a concise commercial redline that should make execution straightforward while protecting both parties operationally:

Key points (proposed):
- Pricing schedule: staged minimum commits over first 12 months (Q1: 250k tokens; Q2: 500k; remainder quarterly as agreed). See attached pricing_schedule_skyforge.xlsx for line items and proration rules.
- Invoice routing: Redwood will issue invoices to the remit-to entity specified on the order form. If multiple remit-to entities are specified, applicable fees will be invoiced to the entity associated with that fee line (e.g., subscription vs services).
- Net terms: standard Net 30; if customer requires Net 45, Redwood may adjust early payment credit and reserve right to apply a 2% late payment fee after 45 days.
- Taxes: each party is responsible for taxes imposed on its own income; customer must provide VAT registration or equivalent for non-US entities. Withholding obligations will be handled as per the invoice routing appendix.
- Change orders & PO: include a clause that reference POs are accepted provided a matching signed order form is provided within 10 business days of PO issuance.

If that looks good I’ll produce a redline PDF and push a clean version into DocuSign for signature routing to the two legal entities.

-Ben

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- The EMEA entity is SkyForge Ltd (UK). We’ll provide the VAT registration for SkyForge Ltd and a W-9 for SkyForge, Inc.
- For invoicing it’s critical that we can present the subscription spend to our US P&L and professional services to the EMEA P&L — can Redwood support separate billing codes on each invoice so our AP team can map them automatically?
- Regarding Net 30 vs Net 45: we are set up as Net 30 but some internal partners route through Net 45 by policy; would Redwood accept Net 30 on subscription and Net 45 on one-off services if that simplifies cashflow?

If you can confirm those three items I’ll get the VAT cert and W-9 uploaded. Also please include a single clause that describes how tax liabilities are calculated if jurisdictions apply VAT or reverse-charge.

—Elena

Hi all — looping in final legal language and operational checklist. Thanks for the details, Elena — please upload the VAT cert and W-9 to the HubSpot deal folder and confirm the exact legal entity names + remit addresses.

Proposed order form appendix language (high level):
\"Invoice Routing & Tax Appendix\":
- Customer shall specify remit-to legal entities on the signature page. Fees shall be apportioned to the remit-to entity corresponding to each fee line item.
- Redwood shall issue invoices to the remit-to entity and include an invoice code to indicate whether the charge is Subscription, Professional Services or One-Time Fees.
- Customer shall provide VAT registration evidence or US tax forms (W-9/W-8BEN) within ten (10) business days of signature. Failure to provide required tax evidence may result in delayed invoice processing and potential withholding as required by law.
- Taxes and withholding: each party remains responsible for taxes on its own income. Where applicable, VAT or reverse charge mechanics will be applied in accordance with the jurisdiction and evidence provided; Redwood will not be responsible for customer-side indirect tax liabilities arising from incorrect information.

Operational checklist:
1) Customer to confirm legal names and remit-to addresses (reply to thread).
2) Customer to upload VAT/W-9 to HubSpot deal (link: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/49831).
3) Redwood to produce a redline order form (Ben) and a DocuSign envelope to two remit-to signatories.
4) Finance to validate invoice codes with customer AP prior to first invoice.

If you confirm the addresses and upload the docs we’ll finalize the redline and push to DocuSign.

Kimberly Park
